llcFilesWith: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division (Application for Registration of Assumed Business Name)
soleProprietorFilesWith: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division (the same application)
feeBasis: The $50 is the Secretary of State's flat fee for a new assumed business name registration, and renewal is another $50 every two years. Filing is at the state level, not the county.
renewalRule: Renew every two years. The renewal application and fee must be filed within the 30 days before each second anniversary of registration; failing to do so is grounds for administrative cancellation of the registration. The Secretary of State must send the registrant's authorized representative a renewal notice at least 30 days before the deadline (ORS 648.017).
protectionNote: Registering an assumed business name discloses who is behind the name; it grants no exclusive right and carries no infringement remedy of its own. It does have a real practical effect: because an active assumed business name is part of the ORS 63.094 distinguishability test, the state will not register a later entity or assumed name that is not distinguishable from it while yours stays current.
searchNote: Oregon keeps assumed business names in the same registry as corporations and LLCs, so the standard Business Name Search returns them alongside entities. An assumed business name appears as an ABN row with its own active or inactive status.
notes: Oregon runs a clean state-level assumed business name system: one $50 filing with the Secretary of State, renewable every two years, indexed in the same registry as entities. Unlike states that record DBAs at the county with no central index, Oregon's assumed names are searchable statewide in the same tool as companies and are screened for distinguishability along with them. One detail the state level hides: ORS 648.007(1) frames the duty county by county, and ORS 648.010(2)(c) makes the application list every county where the applicant intends to do business, so the single state filing still has to name its counties. A service mark used without conspicuously disclosing the filer's real name must itself be registered as an assumed business name. The Oregon Legislature publishes the ORS one chapter per page, so the citation below lands on chapter 648 and the sections are found within it.
